newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officials stay mum on '97 Japan PGM talks.
newsitem.headline: Russian officials stay mum on '97 Japan PGM talks.

text.p: Russian precious metals officials remained tight-lipped on Monday on what agreements, if any, they had struck with Japan, the world's biggest importer of platinum and palladium.

Almazjuvelirexport, Russia's sole export agent of platinum group metals, confirmed that both Vitaly Berlin and Andrei Travkin, in Tokyo for talks with Japanese clients earlier this month, had returned to Moscow.
But neither would comment on the talks, Almaz representatives said.
"Vitaly Berlin is not prepared to comment on the results of the talks," his secretary said. "(Andrei) Travkin is unavailable for comment at the moment," another official added.
Vladimir Rybkin, head of the precious metals and stones department at the Finance Ministry, also declined to comment on the talks or on Russia's platinum and palladium export intentions this year.
"I cannot comment at all on exports (of platinum and palladium) this year," he said.

Russian, the world's largest supplier of palladium and its second biggest platinum exporter, had not made any 1997 deliveries to Japan as at the start of this month after bureaucratic delays and political changes in Russia held up talks between the two sides.
Berlin said from Tokyo earlier this month that Russia would be in a position to resume platinum group metal exports to Japan later in June.
Rybkin, also earlier in June, said from Moscow that Russia's 1997 PGM exports would be slightly down on 1996 levels.
World palladium and platinum prices have soared in recent months, partly on supply delays from Russia.
Confusion spread further on international precious metals markets on Monday on as traders reported a visit to Japan last week by officials of U.S.-based hedge fund Tiger Management.
The fund is believed to be holding a massive amount of palladium through speculative futures trade.
But most traders who met with the fund said they were not interested in buying palladium as they had already signed contracts to buy PGMs from Russia this year under long-term contracts.
